summary: According to a new report from Chinese market research firm Sigmaintell, Samsung Display supplies more than 70% of the OLED panels used by the major laptop brands. summary: iQOO announced that it's upcoming Neo 12 smartphone will be the first phone to adopt Visionox's new pTSF OLED display materials. title: Nvidia rejects near-term memory glut fears, leaves CXMT cooperation open
summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said the company did not expect memory supply to exceed demand in the coming years and remained open to working with China's ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT). The comments, made during the GTC Berlin conference and reported by CNBC, came as falling market valuations for memory manufacturers and new Chinese dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) developments intensified concerns about oversupply.

title: SpaceX's 80,000-site push turns Starlink from satellite overlay into full mobile challenger
summary: SpaceX has firmly established itself in direct-to-device connectivity through Starlink's expanding satellite constellation. But the space giant is now pushing beyond orbital coverage as it seeks an equally consequential position in terrestrial mobile infrastructure.

title: Bosch to spin off automotive business as Asian rivals intensify pressure
summary: Bosch Group plans to establish Bosch Mobility as a wholly owned, legally independent subsidiary in August 2027, separating the business that generated about 60% of group revenue. The move will complete the restructuring of Bosch's four major business areas and leave the parent company focused on strategic oversight and centralized research and development.

title: AIDC launches Taiwan's largest industrial microgrid with 9MW/54MWh energy storage capacity
summary: Aerospace Industrial Development Corporation (AIDC) held an inauguration ceremony for its 9MW/54MWh large-scale microgrid system at its Shuinan facility in Taichung on October 22, marking the official commissioning of what the company describes as Taiwan's largest industrial behind-the-meter energy storage microgrid.

title: LGES Poland plant nears breakeven as utilization rebounds
summary: LG Energy Solution (LGES)'s Wroclaw plant in Poland, long viewed as a major drag on the business, is nearing profitability after posting an operating loss of nearly KRW600 billion (approximately US$430 million) in 2025. A surge in European EV demand and the early conversion of some production lines to energy storage system (ESS) applications have lifted utilization, putting the plant on track to return to profit in the fourth quarter of 2026.

title: Doosan Robotics targets automakers, chipmakers as Chinese rivals cut prices
summary: Doosan Robotics is focusing its sales efforts on large automotive and semiconductor manufacturers as it develops AI-powered systems capable of handling more complex factory tasks, Hyeonchang Jeon, senior manager of the company's Korea sales team, said in an interview with DIGITIMES at FIX 2026 in Daegu, South Korea.

title: Taiwan's inaugural semiconductor strike pauses as nearly 70% of Micron Taoyuan Union rejects new bonus offer
summary: Taiwan's first-ever strike in the semiconductor industry has temporarily drawn to a close. A 24-hour warning strike spearheaded by Micron Technology's Taoyuan union concluded on the morning of October 23, 2026. During the action, an internal ballot saw nearly 70% of all union members sign statements opposing management's proposed compensation structure. Formal labor-management negotiations are set to resume on October 27.

title: Semco's 61-week MLCC lead times give suppliers upper hand in AI supply chain
summary: Samsung Electro-Mechanics (Semco) is gaining pricing power as AI server demand extends multilayer ceramic capacitor (MLCC) lead times beyond a year. Shortages now span consumer, automotive and industrial products, prompting customers to secure 2027 supplies.

title: Lenovo mounts AI comeback with Nvidia Vera Rubin NVL72 deliveries and US plant expansion
summary: More than 30 years ago, Lenovo set out with a vision to bring personal computers into every household. Today, Chairman and CEO Yuanqing Yang has defined a new mission for the 42-year-old tech giant: bring artificial intelligence to every home and industry, while transforming Lenovo into an AI-native enterprise targeting over US$100 billion in annual revenue within two years.

title: Chinese luxury carmakers face barriers in Europe's premium market
summary: Chinese luxury carmakers are expanding in Europe but face barriers that differ from those in China. Brand recognition, sales and repair networks, financing, leasing, and used-car values could slow progress, while established German manufacturers retain most of Europe's premium market. The Chinese carmakers' efforts will test whether technology can overcome entrenched expectations.

title: Japan targets 2nm medical AI chip with IBM design, Rapidus eyed for foundry
summary: Japan's Leading-edge Semiconductor Technology Center (LSTC), Hokkaido University, Fujifilm Corporation, GE HealthCare Japan, and imec announced a joint initiative in Tokyo on October 20 to develop a next-generation medical imaging system powered by a dedicated 2nm AI inference chip. The initiative aims to dramatically accelerate image processing efficiency and enable real-time computing directly on medical equipment.

title: Nvidia B300 chips reportedly surface on China Telecom-linked network, raising export-control questions
summary: Israeli security firm Lava identified 32 Nvidia Blackwell Ultra B300 GPUs through monitoring endpoints linked to China Telecom, a state-owned carrier. The chips are barred from sale to China under US export controls. The finding adds to questions about whether the restrictions can keep advanced AI processors out of the country, but the network data does not establish where the GPUs are physically located.

title: First chip-level device on the list: US FCC bans two devices with Huawei HiSilicon chips under new rule
summary: The US Federal Communications Commission (FCC) has banned two electronic devices from entering the US market because both contain surveillance chips made by Huawei's HiSilicon. The move marks the first time the FCC has used a new rule targeting devices whose chipmakers are deemed national security risks.

title: Samsung reportedly orders final tools for first Taylor fab as Texas site nears 2nm output cap
summary: Samsung Electronics has ordered additional equipment to fill the remaining space at its first foundry fab in Taylor, Texas, a move that would lift the plant's 2nm capacity to 20,000 wafers per month in the second half of 2027, ZDNet Korea reported on October 23, citing industry sources.

title: Taiwan's top telecom spins off AI surveillance unit, plans global push with local hardware makers
summary: Chunghwa Telecom (CHT) has established a new subsidiary, CHT Intelligent Vision Solutions (IVS), spinning off an internal team focused on smart security and intelligent video analytics. The new company will target enterprise security, public safety, and smart-city applications, while taking Taiwanese hardware partners overseas.

title: Apple reportedly taps BOE for LCD iMac development, keeps OLED timetable in question
summary: Apple has reportedly asked BOE Technology and other panel makers for technical information on LCD panels for a future iMac, raising questions about the pace of its OLED transition. The potential LCD model's launch around 2029 overlaps with industry expectations for the first OLED iMac in 2029-2030.

title: TSMC advances CoPoS packaging at Taoyuan Longtan site
summary: TSMC's Longtan Science Park Phase 3 in Taoyuan is restarting after nearly three years of delays, with Taiwan's National Development Council approving its development plan on September 17, 2026. The 104.65-hectare site is expected to focus first on advanced packaging technologies such as CoPoS, joining TSMC's Chiayi AP7 and Southern Taiwan Science Park AP8 facilities as the company expands capacity to meet surging AI demand.

title: Rapidus courts US AI customers ahead of planned 2H27 2nm mass production
summary: Rapidus chairman Tetsuro Higashi said the Japanese chipmaker remains broadly on track to begin mass production of 2nm chips in the second half of 2027. Winning customers remains a key challenge, and initial demand is expected to come mainly from the United States, where demand related to artificial intelligence is strong.

title: Commentary: How long can the humanoid robot bubble last? Unitree's valuation correction puts physical AI to the test
summary: Concerns over a potential AI bubble are intensifying. From large language models (LLMs) and AI data centers to humanoid robots, investors are increasingly questioning when massive capital investments will translate into corresponding revenue and profits.

summary: Chinese smartphone brands have brought high-refresh-rate OLED displays to market ahead of Samsung Electronics and Apple, with Visionox and BOE supplying 185Hz panels for the iQOO Neo 12 and RedMagic 12 Pro+, respectively. The move sets a new standard for smartphone applications, where power consumption remains a major concern, and has drawn market attention.
